items.title: PACMI: Provenance-Aware Cascading Memory Invalidation for Long-Term LLM Agents
items.summary_1line: LLM agents rely on long-term memory to retain and reuse information when performing tasks over long horizons. Existing methods provide limited support for handling memories that become outdated as new observations or...
items.editor_note: Adds provenance-aware invalidation for memories that go stale.

editorial.tldr: Agent memory research started with how to store conversational memory: AutoViewMem proposed self-configuring views instead of fixed granularities. A benchmark post then asked how to evaluate long-term memory beyond the context window.
editorial.whats_new: PACMI (Oct 5) tackles stale memory: it invalidates dependent memories when an upstream fact is outdated, tracked through provenance.
editorial.why_it_matters: Agents that persist memory across sessions need an update and invalidation policy, not only a retrieval layer; stale memories are a reliability risk that retrieval benchmarks do not catch.
editorial.take_for_builders: If your agent persists memory across sessions, record where each memory came from and test that correcting one fact also retires memories derived from it.

status.detail: Research focus is moving from how to store memory to how to keep it correct and measure it.
